articles.title: Cango Inc. Q2 2026 Earnings Call Summary
articles.summary: Moby summary of Cango Inc.'s Q2 2026 earnings call
articles.body:
Strategic Transition and Operational Optimization

Our analysts just identified a stock with the potential to be the next Nvidia. Tell us how you invest and we'll show you why it's our #1 pick. Tap here.

Management deliberately scaled back mining operations to prioritize economic returns over pure scale, resulting in a sequential revenue decline.

The company transitioned a portion of its capacity to a leasing model, shifting direct operating costs and variable risk to lessees.

Operational efficiency was improved by phasing out older S19 series mining machines in favor of newer, more efficient hardware.

A new Bitcoin hedging program was implemented to mitigate price volatility and enhance the predictability of operating cash flows.

The AI infrastructure business moved from technical validation to commercialization following the completion of the Georgia LN site and the signing of the first customer contract.

Management is pursuing a dual-track AI strategy involving both bare-metal GPU hosting and colocation to maximize infrastructure utilization.

Mining and AI are being managed as parallel businesses, with capital allocation focused on sites that offer the best marginal economics.

Infrastructure Expansion and Revenue Outlook

AI-related revenue is expected to begin appearing in third-quarter results, though initial contributions are characterized as modest.

Management anticipates mining hashrate will remain relatively stable in the third quarter, though regional power curtailment during summer months remains a variable.

Future AI expansion includes evaluating new sites and potential self-build options beyond the current 50-megawatt Georgia facility.

The company plans to continue using its BTC-denominated loan structure as a risk management tool to hedge future production.

Strategic focus for the second half of 2026 remains on executing AI deployments and optimizing the mix between self-mining and leased hashrate.

Asset Restructuring and Financial Adjustments

A net loss of $81.6 million was primarily driven by $51.4 million in non-cash impairment and disposal losses related to the mining machine fleet restructuring.

The company recorded a $4.1 million loss from changes in the fair value of crypto assets, which was significantly mitigated by the new hedging program compared to the prior quarter.

Average cash mining cost decreased by 5% sequentially to $73,313 per Bitcoin due to renegotiated hosting contracts with price-reduction mechanisms.

As of June 30, the company held 1,056 Bitcoins and maintained a total liquidity position of approximately $23 million in cash and cryptocurrencies.

articles.title: How Is AT&T's Stock Performance Compared to Telecom Services Stocks
articles.summary: AT&T has lagged behind other telecom services stocks, and analysts remain moderately optimistic about the stock’s outlook.
articles.body:
Dallas, Texas-based AT&T Inc. (T) provides telecommunications and technology services worldwide. The company has a market cap of $177.4 billion and operates through two segments, Communications and Latin America, and offers wireless voice and data communications services, as well as sales of handsets, wireless data cards, wireless computing devices, carrying cases/protective covers, and wireless chargers, and more.

Companies with a market cap of $10 billion or more are typically referred to as "large-cap stocks." T fits squarely into that category, with its market cap exceeding this threshold and reflecting its substantial size and influence in the telecom services industry.

Despite that, the stock currently trades 13.1% below its 52-week high of $29.79, recorded on Sept. 15, 2025. T stock has grown 4.4% over the past three months, outperforming the State Street Communication Services Select Sector SPDR ETF's (XLC) 3.7% decline during the same time frame.

In the longer term, T has delivered a different performance. The stock has declined 10.5% over the past 52 weeks, lagging behind the marginal fall of XLC over the same period. T has been trading above its 200-day moving average since August and also above its 50-day moving average since late July, showcasing bullish momentum.

On July 23, T stock declined marginally following the release of its mixed Q2 2026 earnings. The company's revenue for the quarter amounted to $31.6 billion, which missed Wall Street's forecasts. However, its adjusted EPS for the period came in at $0.65, surpassing the Street's estimates. AT&T expects full-year earnings in the range of $2.25 to $2.35 per share.

When stacked against its rival, Verizon Communications Inc. (VZ) has surged 13.9% over the past year, rallying T.

Wall Street has a moderately optimistic view of the stock currently. Among the 29 analysts tracking T, the overall consensus stands at a "Moderate Buy." Its mean price target of $28.97 suggests 11.9% upside potential from current price levels.

articles.title: Partners Group replaces CEO as it works through evergreen fund redemptions
articles.summary: Partners Group is replacing its CEO after reporting mixed interim results amid redemption pressure on its evergreen products. David Layton, who has been the...
articles.body:
Partners Group is replacing its CEO after reporting mixed interim results amid redemption pressure on its evergreen products.

David Layton, who has been the sole CEO since 2021 and with the firm since 2005, will step down to become CIO and chair of the global investment committee.

Roberto Cagnati and Juri Jenkner, both hired in 2004, will take over as co-CEOs Jan. 1.

Cagnati most recently ran portfolio solutions and served as chief risk officer, while Jenkner most recently served as president after heading both infrastructure and private credit earlier.

The change comes as Partners, which manages total assets of $186 billion, announces mixed interim results. While the group saw record fundraising—with clients committing $16 billion to the firm, up from $12.2 billion a year earlier— profit fell 13% to 502 million Swiss francs (about $620 million).

The inflows contrast with a broader retreat in European PE, where both the total capital raised and number of fund closes have fallen sharply since 2024, according to PitchBook data, with this year on course to be one of the leanest fundraising years in a decade.

Performance income, which also includes investment and interest results, represented 19% of total revenue, below the firm's 2026 guidance of 20-25%—a range it cut this quarter from an earlier target of 25-40%.

The firm expects some exit processes to be postponed into 2027.

"Sometimes it can be a little bit more complex today, and things can get dragged out a little bit. We have a handful of processes that we're just not sure if we'll end up closing and getting the cash this year, or if it's going to be pushed to next year," Layton said on the firm's earnings call.

"At this point in the year, if you're not already signed and marching towards exit, there's just uncertainty there."

The generation of performance fees in evergreen products was also affected by weaker performance in select mature PE portfolios in H1.

Partners Group's share price has fallen more than 30% year to date amid redemption pressure in its evergreen products, which the firm expects to continue.

"There have been a lot of investors that made a lot of money in these funds. The early investors that made five times and when there's questions around the outlook, some people maybe like to buy some of the sort of more fancy public stocks. Some people might have this more thematic investment. So there's all kind of reasons why people try to harvest some of their returns," said executive chairman Steffen Meister in the earnings call.

"Given the sizes of these funds and the fact that we have a little bit more quiet environment, you will see these limitations on liquidity being enacted for a few quarters."

Opus Genetics Inc (NASDAQ:IRD) shares rose 5.9% in pre-market trading ahead of the scheduled release of three-month topline data from Cohort 1 of its OPGx-BEST1 Phase 1/2 clinical trial.

The September 1, 2026 data release concerns OPGx-BEST1, a gene replacement therapy being evaluated in patients with Best Vitelliform Macular Dystrophy and Autosomal-Recessive Bestrophinopathy, two inherited retinal diseases.

The clinical update has previously been identified by analysts covering Opus Genetics as an important development for the programme. The outcome of the trial remains uncertain pending publication of the results.

Analysts focus on OPGx-BEST1 clinical programme

BTIG and B. Riley currently have "Buy" ratings on Opus Genetics with price targets of $12 and $10, respectively, according to the supplied information.

Cantor Fitzgerald has also reiterated a "Buy" rating on the stock. The analysts have identified the OPGx-BEST1 data as an important potential milestone for the company.

Analyst ratings and price targets represent the respective firms' assessments and do not indicate either the outcome of the clinical trial or future share-price performance.

Opus Genetics advances OPGx-LCA5 programme

Elsewhere in its clinical pipeline, Opus Genetics completed enrolment in its registrational Phase 3 trial of OPGx-LCA5 in early August.

The programme represents another gene therapy candidate being advanced by the clinical-stage company alongside OPGx-BEST1.

Progress across the programmes remains subject to clinical trial results and applicable regulatory processes.

Shares advance as broader U.S. markets decline

Opus Genetics' pre-market increase came as the major U.S. equity indices traded lower amid renewed geopolitical tensions between the United States and Iran, higher oil prices and changing expectations for Federal Reserve monetary policy.

The S&P 500, Dow Jones and Nasdaq were all indicated lower ahead of the opening bell.

While the timing of the share-price increase coincides with the scheduled OPGx-BEST1 clinical update, the information provided does not establish the extent to which positioning ahead of the data release caused Tuesday's 5.9% move.

Attention remains focused on the three-month Cohort 1 results as investors await further information on the safety and clinical performance of the OPGx-BEST1 programme.

ShipStation, a provider of multicarrier parcel shipping software, is offering e-commerce sellers the ability to also select and coordinate with less-than-truckload operators at pre-negotiated rates in one integrated platform, bringing to life promised benefits from ownership's recent acquisition of freight brokerage Worldwide Express Group.

Few, if any, software-as-a-service companies that connect small-and-midsize merchants with parcel carriers offer a pallet-shipping solution.

"Most of those small companies don't have enough volumes to do full truckload so their first need after parcel shipping tends to be LTL, which creates this natural linkage between LTL freight brokerage and parcel," said Chris Wofford, the founder of Wofford Advisors LLC, a strategic advisory firm for the logistics sector.

In early June, private equity firm Thoma Bravo acquired WWEX Group and merged it with portfolio company Auctane, which provides shipping and fulfillment technology through brands like ShipStation, Stamps.com, Metapack and Packlink. The combined valuation of the companies is $12 billion.

WWEX Group companies include Worldwide Express, GlobalTranz, Unishippers, JEAR Logistics and BLX Logistics.

WWEX is a UPS parcel reseller to small businesses, a segment the logistics giant has targeted for growth opportunities. WWEX manages customer shipments flowing to UPS under a favorable contract and UPS takes over the account once a customer crosses a certain size. In addition to brokering parcels, WWEX gets rates from trucking companies and sells them to smaller shippers.

Companies like ShipStation manage e-commerce orders from checkout to delivery, providing the companies ability to select carriers based on rates, transit time and other features; create detailed picklists and batch shipping manifests; print shipping labels and track shipments. Manufacturers also use ShipStation.

Other companies that allow retailers to compare and access pre-negotiated discount rates with parcel carriers through software services include Shippo, EasyShip, Pirate Ship and Amazon's Veeqo.

Management, in June, touted that the combined company — now operating under the name ShipStation Global — would allow customers to easily combine order management and parcel, LTL, truckload and global shipping services in a single interface, simplifying the process of managing logistics across multiple vendors. WWEX has more than 75 LTL carriers in its network and more than 50 of them are accessible in the ShipStation ecosystem.

articles.title: Marvell Technology Posts Lower FCF Margins, But Revenue Is Could Surge Next Year - Is MRVL Stock Too Cheap?
articles.summary: Marvell Technology, the custom system-on-a-chip designer, had lower-than-expected FCF and FCF margins, as in Q1. Nevertheless, revenue is expected to surge n...
articles.body:
Marvell Technology (MRVL) , the custom system-on-a-chip designer, had lower-than-expected Q2 FCF and FCF margins, as in Q1. Nevertheless, analysts expect revenue to surge over 51% next year. As a result, MRVL stock could have over 34% upside using conservative FCF margin and FCF yield analysis.

MRVL closed down over 2.2% on Monday, Aug. 31, at $211.66 . That's below its pre-earnings release peak of $251.01 on Aug. 20.

Marvell Technology's Aug. 27 Q2 earnings release shows revenue was higher than expected, according to Seeking Alpha, but earnings per share were just 1 cent better than forecasts.

As Barchart reported, its record growth in revenue and earnings was propelled by data center demand, which is expected to stay strong.

But here is why I think the stock is down. Free cash flow (FCF), FCF growth, and FCF margins were much lower than the high performance achieved in Q1. In short, the market was disappointed that the company didn't repeat these high growth rates and margins.

Marvell Technology doesn't report its FCF numbers. But Stock Analysis data shows that in Q2 it generated $478.8 million, compared to $414.1 million a year ago. That was 15.62% higher. However, in Q1, FCF growth YoY was higher at 125.6%.

Moreover, compared to last year's Q2, the FCF margin was lower. For example, in Q2, its FCF as a percent of revenue was 17.48% compared to 20.64% a year ago, and 19.98% in Q1.

The culprit was flat operating cash flow compared to Q1 and high capex requirements. For example, operating cash flow was $605 million in Q2 vs. $638.8 million in Q1. Investors don't like to see lower OCF, especially when revenue was higher in Q2 (i.e., $9.45 billion, +8.4% in Q2 over Q1 8.717 billion).

The point is that this has led to fears about ongoing OCF and FCF margins. But is this overdone?

For one, over the past year, as of Q2, its FCF margins have remained strong. For example, Stock Analysis reports that the trailing 12-month (TTM) FCF margin in Q2 was 18.31%. That's only slightly lower than the Q1 TTM FCF margin of 19.11%, but much higher than the 17.04% 2026 FCF margin.

articles.summary: Secretário de Energia americano prevê que produção da Venezuela supere 2 milhões de barris por dia até 2030; Chevron anuncia investimento de US$ 7 bilhões para mais que dobrar sua produção no país
articles.body:
A produção de petróleo da Venezuela deve mais que dobrar até 2030 e superar 2 milhões de barris por dia, afirmou nesta quarta-feira (2) o secretário de Energia dos Estados Unidos, Chris Wright. Segundo ele, o país já produz mais de 1,2 milhão de barris por dia.

Wright também disse estar confiante de que o petróleo venezuelano poderá ser usado para recompor a reserva estratégica dos Estados Unidos, um estoque mantido pelo governo americano para situações de emergência no abastecimento.

“Começamos com um pouco menos de um milhão de barris por dia. Hoje, são mais de 1,2 milhão de barris por dia”, afirmou Wright em entrevista à CNBC. “A produção da Venezuela ultrapassará 2 milhões de barris por dia até o final desta década”, acrescentou.

A previsão ocorre após um acordo entre os Estados Unidos e a Venezuela que amplia a participação americana no setor de petróleo do país. Wright está em Caracas nesta quarta-feira para acompanhar a assinatura de novos acordos com o governo interino de Delcy Rodríguez.

O acordo dá aos Estados Unidos o direito de explorar um quinto das reservas de petróleo da Venezuela , de acordo com os termos divulgados sobre a negociação.

EUA ampliam presença no petróleo venezuelano

Wright afirmou que a participação do governo americano aumenta a segurança e a confiança nos contratos e pode ajudar a atrair investimentos para o setor de petróleo da Venezuela.

O país passou por anos de queda na produção e dificuldades na indústria petrolífera. No início deste ano, o governo de Delcy Rodríguez promoveu uma reforma da Lei de Hidrocarbonetos, que facilita a criação de novos negócios no setor.

A expectativa americana é que a mudança nas regras e a entrada de investimentos ajudem a acelerar a recuperação da produção venezuelana.

A Chevron, uma das maiores petrolíferas americanas, anunciou nesta quarta-feira que pretende investir mais de US$ 7 bilhões na Venezuela nos próximos cinco anos.

A empresa americana prevê mais que dobrar sua produção no país, chegando a cerca de 600 mil barris por dia.

Chevron, Eni, KEO Capital e Primavera estão entre as empresas envolvidas em novos acordos de energia com o governo venezuelano. Os contratos preveem, principalmente, a expansão de projetos negociados com o Ministério do Petróleo e com a PDVSA, a estatal venezuelana de petróleo.

Os novos acordos seguem as regras da reforma aprovada em janeiro.

A KEO Capital, por meio de sua subsidiária nos Estados Unidos, fechou um acordo com a PDVSA para formar a joint venture Petrourdaneta. A empresa ficará responsável pela operação do projeto e terá uma linha de crédito de US$ 350 milhões.

A italiana Eni também pretende ampliar sua atuação na Venezuela com uma nova área na Faixa do Orinoco, uma das principais regiões produtoras de petróleo do país.

O movimento ocorre depois de anos de afastamento de grandes empresas americanas do setor de petróleo venezuelano.

ExxonMobil e ConocoPhillips deixaram projetos no país após a nacionalização de ativos em 2007. A Chevron permaneceu na Venezuela e agora planeja ampliar sua produção.

A Venezuela tem as maiores reservas de petróleo do mundo. A indústria do país, porém, foi enfraquecida por problemas de gestão, corrupção e sanções.

Além do aumento da produção venezuelana, Wright vê o petróleo do país como uma possível fonte para recompor a reserva estratégica americana.

A reserva estratégica é um estoque de petróleo mantido pelo governo dos Estados Unidos para ser usado em situações de emergência, como interrupções no fornecimento.

Wright disse estar confiante de que o petróleo venezuelano poderá ser trocado por petróleo destinado à reserva americana.

Em outra declaração nesta quarta-feira, o secretário afirmou que espera que a Venezuela produza mais de 1,5 milhão de barris por dia já no primeiro semestre de 2027.

A previsão é de que a produção continue crescendo até superar 2 milhões de barris por dia no fim da década.

articles.title: Range Rover goes electric as clients say they want $138K SUV 'in a fully electric form,' exec says
articles.summary: The Range Rover Electric, which starts at around $138,000 in the US, arrives as American demand for high-end EVs remains soft.
articles.body:
Range Rover finally revealed its first EV, the Range Rover Electric, a car that starts at around $138,000 in the US (£154,070) and arrives as American demand for EVs remains soft.

The Range Rover Electric looks just like its gas-powered brethren, and that appears to be on purpose — to reassure the faithful that this is indeed a fully capable Range Rover. Twin 260kW permanent magnet motors make up to 550PS (543hp) and 850Nm of torque — "V8 levels of power," in the company's phrase — yet run nearly silent, with 0-60 mph in as little as 4.3 seconds.

"Range Rover clients have been telling us for some time that they want an electric Range Rover, but only if it delivers the same uncompromising experience they expect from the brand," Martin Limpert, Range Rover managing director, told Yahoo Finance. "That means effortless performance, refined comfort, all-terrain capability, and the sense of calm our clients value."

Capability-wise, the Electric can ford up to nearly three feet of water and climb 45-degree slopes using single-pedal driving. It features a traction system that reacts within 50 milliseconds, around 100 times faster than a gas-powered Range Rover, the company said.

The Electric uses a 118.5kWh double-stacked lithium-ion battery using 800-volt architecture, good for an estimated 372 miles of range (not EPA-certified yet). On charging, Range Rover said a 10%-80% charge takes only 22 minutes, and 137 miles can be added in as little as 10 minutes at peak rate. Notably for the US, a native North American Charging Standard (NACS) port comes standard, meaning Tesla's Supercharger network is available.

On the negative side, while the Electric's range is decent, it still lags behind many of its rivals.

"Our research shows that many Range Rover clients' driving patterns are already highly compatible with electric vehicle ownership," Limpert countered, adding that most will be charging at home, blunting the effects of range anxiety.

In the US, Range Rover's EV will cost more than rivals like the Cadillac ( GM ) Escalade IQ (about $127,000), the Mercedes ( MBGAF ) EQS SUV (about $91,000), and the Lucid ( LCID ) Gravity (from about $80,000).

Along with its exterior styling and on- and off-road capability, the cabin interior is where Range Rover makes the case on price, as it is positioned as a luxury offering. Range Rover said the Electric rides on twin-chamber air suspension that is quieter and more refined than any previous Range Rover, and it comes with an interior fridge as well as a fold-out for enjoying drinks alfresco, perhaps at a polo event. (At least that's what Range Rover would like its clients to imagine.)

articles.title: Nation’s largest school district bans AI in the classroom through 8th grade
articles.summary: New York City is banning the use of generative artificial intelligence for public school students from 2K through 8th grade, part of a larger move to restrict classroom technology in the nation’s largest school district.
articles.body: New York City is banning the use of generative artificial intelligence for public school students from 2K through 8th grade, part of a larger move to restrict classroom technology in the nation’s largest school district. The one-year moratorium will affect nearly 600,000 public school students, nearly two-thirds of the district’s total enrollment. As part of the policy rollout, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said the district will “discontinue or disable the AI components of more than 38 previously allowed programs that do not meet our new safety and oversight standards.” Mamdani announced the policy on Wednesday with New York City Schools Chancellor Kamar Samuels, saying it’s designed to protect students’ critical thinking abilities as well as the relationships between students and teachers. Many communities across the country have pushed for stricter limits on screentime and AI use, amid growing fears that the technology could stunt students’ learning and development or pose safety risks. Meanwhile, AI companies have rolled out tools for learning and education, and provided funding to teachers’ unions to help develop AI training curricula. The Los Angeles Unified School District this year announced major restrictions on classroom screen use, and New York state last year banned students from using personal phones during the school day. But Mamdani’s office called Wednesday’s announcement the country’s “most expansive” limits around AI use in schools. In New York City, the education department banned the use of ChatGPT from school devices and networks in 2023, before reversing course months later. Under the policy announced Wednesday, a new Technology in Schools Coalition of educators, parents, students and others will evaluate the impacts of the moratorium and make recommendations for future school years. New York City high school students will have access to a limited slate of AI tools and receive “AI critical thinking” courses. Companion chatbots, as well as mainstream services such as ChatGPT and Claude, will be blocked for all grades. The district will also limit individual screen time for students based on grade level. The policy includes exceptions for students with disabilities and English learners. Teachers will be allowed to use AI for lesson planning and other “operational tasks,” but not for grading or student assessments. Michael Mulgrew, president of the New York-based United Federation of Teachers, lauded the screentime limits and carve-outs for students with special needs in a statement Wednesday. But he questioned how the education department will evaluate learning tools’ AI safeguards going forward, saying schools or educators could be left uncertain about which products are approved for use. Samuels on Wednesday acknowledged the challenge of preventing students from using AI at home, for example, to help complete homework. He said the policy “seeks to expand our teachers’ and our understanding of how to combat the external use of AI,” but also called on parents to help monitor their kids’ tech use at home. Still, Mamdani said he believes the policy will benefit students and educators. “The tech industry wants us to believe that AI in early education is not only inevitable, but that it is necessary,” Mamdani said during Wednesday’s press conference. “We do not see it that way.” CNN’s Katherine Koretski contributed to this report.

images.caption: Schools Chancellor Kamar Samuels and Mayor Zohran Mamdani announce new restrictions on screen time and AI use for New York City public school students on September 2, 2026.

articles.title: Divide between energy trackers and the White House deepens over how much oil is getting through the Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: This Monday in the Strait of Hormuz was either a great or terrible day for the global economy as the estimates from commercial trackers and the White House a...
articles.body:
This Monday in the Strait of Hormuz was either a great or terrible day for the global economy, depending on whom you ask.

Ship-tracking service Kpler reported that "traffic declined sharply," with just five ships crossing on Monday, the same day that the US and Iran exchanged fire for the first time in a month . The data platform documented a mix of official ships as well as shadow vessels using concealment tactics.

Yet the picture from the Trump administration couldn't have been more different, with Energy Secretary Chris Wright saying in a CNBC interview that over 17 million barrels of oil passed through the waterway on Monday. Wright called it a record since the beginning of the conflict.

Wright's figures are rooted in claims from the Trump administration that dozens of ships are being assisted by the US Navy each night, undetected by commercial shipping trackers. Kpler and others use satellite imagery and other tools to gauge traffic in the waterway that is about 21 miles wide at its narrowest point.

The conflicting data has been evident throughout the summer , growing as a political flash point. Independent statistics have also further irked the White House by undercutting Trump's claims of US control over the waterway.

Meanwhile, tensions between the US and Iran resumed with renewed attacks pushing crude oil prices above $95 a barrel .

President Trump weighed in on Wednesday on Truth Social, again claiming that the US is in control and positing, "Should we change the name Hormuz Strait to TRUMP STRAIT???"

The bluster follows weeks in which Trump and his team have declined to back up their claims, leading to widespread skepticism about the White House's optimistic claims and uncertainty about where the truth lies.

"Might as well just rename it Schrödinger's Strait…" Mason Hamilton, a vice president of economics and research at the American Petroleum Institute, posted on X in reference to a famous thought experiment by Erwin Schrödinger about a (possibly) ill-fated cat.

Multiple sources show single-digit ship crossings

Trump often claims crossings through the strait are even higher than his team puts forth. "We've been averaging 30 ships a night [and] a lot of oil is coming out," he told reporters on Monday.

But weeks of data from a variety of sources suggest far less activity.

The IMF and Oxford University have documented fewer than five oil tanker crossings per day and overall crossing numbers in the single digits for weeks — far below the pre-conflict level of roughly 120 vessels (including dozens of tankers) per day.

articles.title: After Gujarat tender flop, govt seeks UK, Dutch help for offshore wind push
articles.summary: India Business News: NEW DELHI: India is in talks with the UK and the Netherlands for technical expertise in setting up the country’s first offshore wind energy project in.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India is in talks with the UK and the Netherlands for technical expertise in setting up the country’s first offshore wind energy project in Tamil Nadu.A senior official of the ministry of new and renewable energy said geophysical and geotechnical surveys have been conducted to analyse seabed composition, soil stratification and load-bearing capacity for foundations. Discussions have also been held with stakeholders and relevant data collated to support the development of the first 1 GW of offshore capacity.“Since this will be our first such project, we are seeking guidance from experts in the UK, the Netherlands and other European countries on how they approach offshore wind energy development,” said Rajesh Kulhari, joint secretary in the ministry of new and renewable energy.Since the tender floated last year for setting up a project in Gujarat failed to attract any bids, Kulhari said govt was keen to make a second attempt. Speaking on the sidelines of the curtain-raiser of the 8th edition of Windergy India 2026, scheduled to take place on Oct 7-8 in Chennai, he added that the ministry was also evaluating the Gujarat tender to understand why it failed to attract bidders and would seek expert help to make necessary amendments.Offshore wind energy projects currently cost at least four times more than typical onshore projects. High upfront costs, tariff uncertainty, transmission readiness, and port capacity and logistics are some of the factors that deter developers and investors.According to an assessment by the National Institute of Wind Energy, 35 GW of India’s estimated 91 GW offshore wind potential lies off Tamil Nadu’s coastline.While India and the UK have formed a joint offshore taskforce to accelerate strategic clean energy cooperation through time-bound, execution-focused collaboration, the partnership with the Netherlands will also help shape an actionable plan.Kulhari also said India will soon surpass Germany to become the third-largest wind energy producer in the world. articles.title: UK’s Burnham faces first parliament grilling, vows to ‘bring back hope’
articles.summary: Newly appointed leader takes first Prime Minister’s Questions, pledges to fulfill defence, social spending goals.
articles.body:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has faced his first grilling in the House of Commons since replacing his predecessor, Keir Starmer, in July.

Responding to members of Parliament during the so-called Prime Minister’s Questions on Wednesday, Burnham said that the United Kingdom remains fully committed to its military obligations despite growing economic challenges at home.

“We will fully fund the Defence Investment Plan, and at the spending review, we will set out a plan to meet our NATO commitments by 2035,” Burnham said during the questioning, a weekly event often defined by raucous exchanges.

“There is no problem with our commitment to defence,” Burnham said.

The newly appointed prime minister faced the sharpest criticism from opposition Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch, who questioned how the administration plans to fund its extensive commitments as UK government borrowing has soared.

Burnham pushed back, attributing market instability to the economic record of the previous Conservative government. He told lawmakers that his administration is working to balance strict fiscal discipline with urgent relief for families struggling under a severe cost-of-living crisis.

Turning to international security, Burnham made reference to a recent attempted attack on the Leipzig/Halle airport , which the German government has blamed on Russia.

He called on British lawmakers across all parties to stand in complete solidarity with both Germany and Ukraine as regional geopolitical tensions escalate.

The questioning came a day after Burnham faced the House of Commons for the first time since becoming prime minister six weeks ago.

His rise came in the wake of a string of local election defeats under Starmer, who was pushed out as leader of his own Labour Party just two years after winning a landslide 2024 election victory.

Burnham, one of the UK’s best-known regional politicians, who earned the nickname “King of the North” as mayor of Greater Manchester, struck a decidedly hopeful tone.

We can lift the prospects of all our people and places. We can put more power into every postcode,” he said. “We can let Britain believe again. We can bring back hope.”

He further promised to exercise “stronger public control” over essential services, notably energy and water utilities.

Burnham told MPs he will outline his long-term agenda in a 10-year plan for the UK to be released before the end of the year.

The upcoming road map will “set out plans for stronger public control over … essentials, making them work for people and places again,” he said, arguing that the cost of basic services is actively dragging down economic growth.

“Household energy bills are the highest in Europe, and the cost of energy is impacting business and inward investment,” Burnham said.

In one of his first actions since moving to Downing Street, Burnham’s government announced a tax cut on household electricity bills set to take effect next month, alongside relief measures easing tax burdens on pubs and hospitality venues.

“When it comes to the biggest issues facing the country, the economy and the cost-of-living crisis, people are looking for much more substantial change,” Burnham said.

“Britain is not where any of us would wish it to be. Things are not working as they should. Life is too expensive and too hard for too many.”

“This is why this government’s first moves were to give businesses and people a little breathing space,” he added.

articles.body: BENGALURU: IPO-bound Simple Energy estimates monthly demand at 3,000-4,000 scooters but is delivering around 1,500-2,000, leaving a rolling backlog of 2,000-2,200 vehicles, founder and CEO Shreshth Mishra told TOI.“Today, demand is not a problem for us. We have almost double the demand of what we are able to supply,” Mishra said. Customers are typically waiting about a month, he added.The company expects output to begin rising from the end of September or in October. Mishra said recently raised capital was being deployed to expand its manufacturing operations and supplier capacity.His comments came as Simple launched Wave, its first family-focused electric scooter. The lineup has six models across three variants, with battery packs ranging from 2.2kWh to 5kWh and claimed test-cycle ranges of 110km to 243km. Prices start at a little over Rs 1 lakh, while deliveries are scheduled to begin in the last week of September.The entry price applies to the base model. Simple has not disclosed the price of the 5kWh Wave+, which carries the headline 243km range. Mishra said the introductory price would remain for the “foreseeable future”, with detailed variant prices to be released separately.Wave uses the same motor, battery and chassis platform as Simple One, with modifications for a family-scooter layout. Mishra said this allowed the company to develop it faster while using components already tested on vehicles on the road.Simple currently describes its effective production capacity as 3,000 scooters a month. Mishra said the physical plant could make more, but output had been constrained by supplier capacity, the production ramp and the size of its dealership network.Simple has more than 75 exclusive outlets across over 60 cities and is targeting monthly sales of 10,000 scooters by March 2027. It has raised Rs 736 crore to date, including a recent Rs 250-crore debt-and-equity round.Asked about Wave’s Rs 10,000 premium over competitors, Mishra said Simple would compete on value rather than price alone. articles.body: BENGALURU: Chief minister D K Shivakumar on Wednesday urged women entrepreneurs to publicly support his government’s tunnel-road project, saying some political leaders were opposing the plan for political reasons even as Bengaluru’s traffic continued to worsen.Addressing the fifth edition of “Together We Grow,” organised by the Ubuntu Consortium at FKCCI, Shivakumar said the city’s mobility problems were costing businesses and workers both time and money. He asked the gathering to speak up about the issue and hold political leaders accountable.“Even, shout at me if I am doing wrong,” he said, adding that entrepreneurs had a direct stake in improving mobility because employees needed to travel to their establishments and factories.Shivakumar defended the tunnel-road proposal as a necessary response to Bengaluru’s constrained road network. He said widening existing roads was difficult because much of the city had not been planned for its present scale. Travelling from Mysuru to Bengaluru could take about 90 minutes, he said, but entering the city and reaching the final destination could take even longer.He reiterated that the government was investing more than Rs 1.5 lakh crore in Bengaluru’s development and mobility infrastructure. The city’s rapid growth and rising number of vehicles had made travel increasingly difficult, he said.The remarks come amid intensified opposition to the proposed north-south tunnel corridor between Hebbal and Silk Board. The project has faced criticism from the BJP, civic groups and urban-mobility experts. Critics have questioned its cost and argued that car-focused infrastructure could undermine the city’s public-transport goals.Concerns have also been raised over its possible impact on green spaces, particularly Lalbagh. The controversy sharpened after the state legislature passed amendments relating to the use of parkland for public infrastructure and the clearance of large urban-transport projects. He said running a business involved considerable financial stress, including meeting salaries, paying suppliers and servicing loans.“You are not employees. He also called for more educated women to enter politics and assume leadership roles from gram panchayats to Parliament.The chief minister questioned the continued preference for sons in Indian families. articles.title: Trump Says Iran Strikes to Be Short, Asserts Hormuz Control
articles.summary: President Donald Trump said renewed attacks on Iran would likely be short-lived, reiterating his claim that the US controls the crucial Strait of Hormuz afte...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- President Donald Trump said renewed attacks on Iran would likely be short-lived, reiterating his claim that the US controls the crucial Strait of Hormuz after fresh fighting spiked energy prices and rekindled fears of an open-ended war.

Asked on Wednesday how long the bombing campaign could last, Trump told reporters, "I don't think too long." Brent crude eased slightly on his comments to just over $95.

The US military carried out a second round of strikes in three days overnight, targeting radar systems and mine-laying capabilities along Iran's southern coast. Iran retaliated with drone and missile volleys on US bases across the Middle East, in line with a pattern used throughout the six-month war.

"We took out all of the new equipment that they tried to build along the Strait of Hormuz — some defensive, some offensive," Trump said. "It was a very heavy attack last night, and we're prepared to do another one any time we want."

Tehran accused the US of hitting a wedding ceremony in the southern coastal city of Sirik, with the Iranian Red Crescent Society saying at least four people died and about 67 were injured. The organization, which had previously put the number of fatalities at five, said the total may rise.

"The US military never targets civilians," said US Navy Captain Tim Hawkins, a spokesperson for US Central Command, which oversees American forces in the Middle East.

Iranian officials likened the incident to a strike on an elementary school in the city of Minab during the early days of the conflict. That attack killed an estimated 120 children and is under investigation by the US military.

"This cruelty cannot be separated from the chain of atrocities that preceded it in Minab," Iran's Foreign Ministry Spokesman Esmail Baghaei posted on X. "Iran will respond to these savage crimes with firmness."

The resumption of hostilities brought an abrupt end to a month of subdued military activity, during which oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz recovered to roughly half of pre-war levels. The improvement in flows risks being curtailed, affecting supplies of oil, gas and other commodities and boosting energy prices and inflation.

articles.title: Delivery Hero board backs Uber’s $15B takeover bid
articles.summary: If approved, the combined company would become one of the largest food delivery platforms in the world.
articles.body:
Delivery Hero's board has signed off on Uber's $15 billion takeover offer and recommended shareholders approve the deal, which would create one of the largest on-demand food delivery platforms in the world.

After reviewing the offer, Delivery Hero's supervisory and management boards said it was in the best interests of the company, its shareholders, employees, and other stakeholders. The boards also deemed that the price was "fair and adequate" and said the deal had the "potential to accelerate product innovation."

The deal, if approved, would double Uber's global footprint and make its delivery platform one of the largest in the world outside of China. It could also put Uber in a better position to compete with DoorDash and Just Eat Takeaway.

Uber, which was already the largest shareholder in Delivery Hero, set a minimum acceptance threshold of 50%, plus one share of Delivery Hero's outstanding share capital.

Prosus, another major shareholder, has agreed to sell its 17% stake in Delivery Hero as well, according to the announcement. Delivery Hero previously agreed to sell its businesses in 14 markets where Uber Eats already operates to New York-based investment firm SSW Partners for $1.6 billion.

The tie-up is the latest example of consolidation in the on-demand delivery industry. In the past 18 months, Uber agreed to acquire Turkey-based Getir for $335 million , Grab said it would buy Delivery Hero's Foodpanda business in Taiwan for $600 million in cash, and DoorDash said it would pay $3.87 billion for the U.K.'s Deliveroo .

articles.title: Can you tell if your beef is a product of America?
articles.summary: The U.S. is allowing more imported beef into the food supply in an effort to lower prices.
articles.body:
(NEXSTAR) – In an effort to lower beef prices, President Trump announced last month that thousands of additional tons of beef will be allowed into the U.S.

The deal, Trump said, allows up to 300,000 metric tons of ground beef to be imported into the U.S. for the next 90 days without activating an “out of quota” tariff, which is a tax that goes into effect once a certain quantity of that product enters the country. The president said on social media that he had committed to ensuring the imported beef would be sold at 25% below current market rates, making it cheaper for American consumers .

A White House official told The Associated Press that the beef in question is lean beef trimmings that are used for ground beef production.

Trump, however, did not specify where the imported beef is coming from, telling reporters in August that “there are a few countries” that will send the “highest quality beef.”

That may leave you wondering whether the beef you’re buying is American-made or not.

Most of the ground beef made from the imported trimmings will go to food service, specifically fast food restaurants, Dr. Derrell Peel, a professor of agricultural economics and the extension specialist for livestock marketing at Oklahoma State University, told Nexstar via email.

Imported beef generally doesn’t appear in grocery stores, “except when it is specifically labeled,” Peel added, explaining, as an example, that “beef from Mexico is sold and marketed in some grocery stores specifically for Hispanic markets.”

But beef producers can add a “Product of USA” label to their meat, to differentiate their products. To qualify, the animals the product is derived from must have been “exclusively born, raised, harvested, and processed in the United States,” according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture. It can’t include “imported livestock” nor “imported ingredients” if it is a single-ingredient product.

If there are multiple ingredients in the product, however, “every component except spices and flavorings must be sourced from the United States, and all preparation and processing steps must take place within the U.S.”

But, even if the products qualify, the “Product of USA” labels are voluntary, which can make it difficult to identify exclusively American meat from products that have been combined with imported beef.

Imported beef is not uncommon in the U.S. food supply, though. Beef from Canada and Mexico has been “part of our total beef supply for many years,” according to Peel.

This beef may appear in products with labeling that describes it as being “packed” or “processed” in the U.S. Some beef products may also explicitly note their country of origin on their labels.

Beef from Canada and Mexico, as well as Brazil, Australia and New Zealand, comprised of about 80% of the nation’s beef imports through the first half of 2026, Nexstar’s NewsNation reported last week.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: US judge rejects bid to break up Google’s ad business
articles.summary: Justice Department had argued Google could not be trusted to run the online advertising exchange.
articles.body:
Alphabet’s Google has escaped a breakup of its advertising technology business, marking the third time in recent years that United States antitrust enforcers have tried to force a Big Tech breakup and lost.

US Judge Leonie Brinkema in Alexandria, Virginia, on Wednesday declined to make Google sell AdX, where publishers pay Google a 20 percent fee to sell ads in auctions that happen instantly when users load websites.

The US Department of Justice (DOJ) had argued Google could not be trusted to run the online advertising exchange after Brinkema ruled that Google had illegally quashed competition .

The judge accepted behavioural remedies.

The reasoning behind today’s decision was not immediately made public.

Brinkema filed her opinion under seal for 14 days, leaving the details of how Google must change its ad business unknown for now. She gave the two sides 30 days to submit a joint proposed final judgement.

The case focused on Google’s ad tech “stack” – the suite of tools that website publishers use to sell ads and advertisers use to buy them.

Brinkema ruled last year that Google had willfully monopolised both the publisher ad server and ad exchange markets, and had unlawfully tied the two products together.

Google has said it will appeal the underlying liability ruling.

The government’s case portrayed Google as simultaneously controlling multiple sides of the digital advertising marketplace and owning the platform that publishers use to sell ads as well as the exchange where transactions occur – all while commanding huge advertiser demand. Prosecutors had sought the sale of Google’s ad auction site AdX and the open-sourcing of critical auction technology.

Google characterised the proposed remedies as extreme government overreach that would harm publishers, advertisers and consumers. It had also argued that splitting up the service would be technically unfeasible.

AdX is a small part of Google’s business. Google’s shares pared gains slightly after the ruling and were up 0.6 percent.

The company welcomed the court decision. “We’re very pleased the court rejected the DOJ’s proposal to break apart tools that help small businesses reach new customers and grow,” said Google executive Lee-Anne Mulholland.

The DOJ is “pleased that the court ordered substantial relief”, it said in a social media post on X.

“We are one step closer to restoring competition and bringing relief for the American people in online advertising markets. The Department is evaluating appropriate next steps,” the DOJ said.

While Google has been ordered to change some business practices, the ruling is the third time in a row that a judge has rejected a bid by US antitrust enforcers to break up Big Tech.

Sacha Haworth, executive director of The Tech Oversight Project, said the rulings “prove that the courts alone will not save us from Big Tech”. The advocacy group has proposed legislation aimed at restoring competition in digital advertising.

A federal judge in Washington last year rejected an attempt by the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to make Meta Platforms sell off Instagram and WhatsApp, saying the agency failed to prove that Meta holds a monopoly in a social media landscape that has shifted drastically since the case was brought in 2020. The FTC has filed an appeal.

Likewise, another judge in Washington, who previously ruled that Google holds an illegal monopoly in online search, rejected the DOJ’s bid to make the company sell its Chrome browser, citing rising competition from generative artificial intelligence companies such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT.

articles.title: Uber shuts operations in Nigeria and Uganda with immediate effect
articles.summary: Nigeria - Africa's most populous country - is proving a tough market for ride-hailing services.
articles.body:
Uber has announced it is closing its operations in Nigeria - Africa's most populous country - and the East African nation of Uganda with immediate effect

The global ride-hailing giant said it had come to the "difficult decision" after a thorough review of its business. It began operating in Nigeria in 2014 and in Uganda two years later.

Uber taxi drivers in Nigeria have long complained that prices on the app are too low, given the rising cost of fuel, and that commission charges are too high. The company has also faced pressure from rival platforms.

The announcement came as Uber's chief executive, Dara Khosrowshahi, said the company was cutting its global workforce by 10%.

Over the last year, Uber has also pulled out of Ivory Coast and Tanzania. The latest announcement means Egypt, Ghana, Kenya and South Africa are the only African countries in which the firm now operates.

"This decision is limited strictly to these two markets and does not impact our operations across the rest of the continent," Uber's statement to the BBC said.

"We remain committed to sub-Saharan Africa, where we continue to see strong growth and opportunity."

Over its 12 years operating in Nigeria, Uber had expanded its services. In the commercial hub of Lagos, it launched a boat service in 2019 in an effort to help commuters bypass the city's notorious congestion.

Lagos, one of Africa's largest and busiest cities, is infamous for its long traffic jams that cause gridlock and hamper business activity.

Other ride-hailing taxi apps have launched in the West African nation over the last decade, including international competitors such as Bolt and inDrive, as well as a number of local operators.

But the Nigerian market has become increasingly challenging for them all, with drivers staging protests and industrial action in recent years over rising operating costs, low fares and working conditions.

The removal of Nigeria's fuel subsidy after President Bola Tinubu's election in 2023 saw the cost of living rise. The subsidy had kept down the price of petroleum products low for decades.

This year, motorists have been hit again by the rise in petrol prices following the US's war with Iran.

Uganda's Daily Monitor newspaper said Uber's departure would mean a major change for commuters in the capital, Kampala. But it said the void was likely to be filled by other taxi apps such as Faras, Bolt and SafeBoda.

Uber pledged to support employees and drivers affected by the decision and said its help centre would remain open for those in Nigeria and Uganda until 23 September to deal with outstanding issues.
